author: haiku
label: c2-seed-haiku-01
changes: Rewrote the whole file for a newcomer: a summary, a terms list, the Mermaid flow, numbered steps, a failure table, notes and open questions.

Added every fixed requirement from the brief, which the first version only named: PR behaviour, one SHA-tagged image, parallel tests with one integration retry, staging smoke gate, approval by release-approvers with no author approval and a 72-hour expiry, deployment window, one production deploy at a time, canary with a 15-minute 1% watch, and #deploys announcements.

Kept every fact from the first version: PR checks, SHA image, integration retry, all five deploy.sh modes, staging and production locks, approval and 72h timeout, window, canary watch with 1% threshold, kubectl rollout undo, superseding, and #deploys notifications.

Carried over from the existing files what readers need: forward-only migrations, rollback changing only the image and current_tag, tags written only after success, canary never recorded in SSM, the 10% traffic split, and the Prometheus query.
Q1: stated that the pipeline starts on a merge to main and defined the PR checks as today's build and make test-unit with nothing pushed or deployed.
Q2: stated the image location, the SHA tag, and that staging and canary receive the same tag, not a rebuild.
Q3: stated one automatic retry, so two attempts, and the failure path to #deploys.
Q4: defined the two named locks, when each is held and released, and that a waiting run is not failed.
Q5: defined the approval job, the release-approvers group, the author rule and the 72-hour expiry outcome.
Q6: spelled out the canary steps, the traffic share, the 30-second check, the no-data rule and the canary-off and promotion paths.
Q7: defined superseding as a rule tied to taking the staging lock, and kept runs in canary or production from being cancelled.
Q8: split undo from rollback by whether SSM tags were already written, with a one-clause reason, and added the migration and canary cases.
Added the deployment window as a gate before the canary and stated that canary start is the production start.
Added the explicit rejection path and the case where canary-off or rollback itself fails.
Added open questions for queue order, author-block enforcement, promotion after 15:00, approvals held over the window, and the repeated rollback behaviour.
Summary now says how the system works today (a laptop runs deploy.sh and SSM records the tags) before describing the pipeline.
Added terms for Run and Superseded, and clarified the Canary and Stable terms, including the shared production Postgres.
Step 4: any test failure now ends the run and cancels the other suite if running; a unit pass waits for integration.
Step 5 and the diagram: a failed kubectl rollout undo on staging keeps the staging-deploy lock and stops the run.
Step 6: staging-deploy release is explicit (on smoke pass, before approval); a failed rollback keeps the lock.
Step 10: the watch starts at the canary rollout and the first check waits one minute, since the 1-minute rate needs canary samples; no data is defined.
Step 11 and the diagram: production undo runs before tags are written, then canary-off, then the lock is released; a failed canary-off keeps the lock.
Superseding rules: a run holding staging-deploy is never cancelled, cancelled runs hold no lock, at most one run waits for approval, and a newer run that fails tests cancels nothing.
Diagram: waiting states (staging lock, approval, window, production lock) now show the superseded path as dotted edges, and the HOLD box shows where the lock is kept.
Failure table: added a Lock column, and a row for undo, rollback or canary-off commands that fail (lock kept until a person releases it).

Notes: stated that no data means zero canary requests in the last minute and fails the run; added a note that production has no automatic path after promotion; open questions added for low-traffic no-data failures, the post-promotion rollback, and who checks the cluster.
Step 5: the CI job that takes staging-deploy runs deploy.sh with CI's credentials, as the environments file describes (Q17).
Step 10, the WATCH label in the flow diagram, and the canary failure row: a failed query such as Prometheus being unreachable counts as a failed check, the same as no data (Q18).
Step 11: the canary keeps its 2 pods and 10% share through the stable rollout, because deploy.sh production changes only stable (Q19).
Notes: after a staging rollback, the restored build stays on staging until the next deploy, and the next deploy reads current_tag, so previous_tag stays correct (Q20).
Notes: a run stopped with a held lock does not resume, other runs wait with no time limit, and a restart needs a new run (Q21).
Superseding rules: finishing a canary or production run cancels nothing, and a waiting run is cancelled only by a newer run taking staging-deploy (Q22).
Open questions: added the CI credentials or roles for SSM and each cluster (Q17), the missing time limit on a held lock (Q21), and how a stopped run is restarted (Q21).
Added a plain summary that first says how the laptop deploy works today, then how the pipeline changes it.
Added terms a newcomer needs: CI, Kubernetes deployment, rollout, context, load balancer, Prometheus, 5xx rate, manual approval job, HOLD, and a one-line definition of each existing command and tag.
Kept the Mermaid flowchart as drawn, with its notes after it. Its HOLD, superseded and rollout-undo paths are unchanged.
Turned each step into trigger, action, data kept, and failure path, with one short reason where a step needs one. Added the step-11 point that the canary keeps its share during the stable rollout.

Merged the duplicated concurrency statements (superseding, lock holder, canary/production runs, cancelled runs not posted, waiting for production-deploy) into one rules list. Removed the separate flow paragraph about dotted lines.
Stated the undo-versus-rollback choice once, in Notes. Steps and the table point to the rule instead of repeating it.
Moved the staging-rollback leftover detail (previous build stays on staging, cancelled build can be restored but not approved) into Notes, stated once.
Added a short Setup section for what CI must provide, kept apart from how a run behaves.

Merged the manual re-run question into the HOLD open question, and kept every open question from the first version. Added the open questions for who releases a held lock and which credentials run deploy.sh.

Cut no requirement, limit, number or setting from the first version or the brief. The document is longer than the first version because the brief requires a full flow, failure table and rules, which the first version did not have.
holes: Q12: What does the `previous_tag` rollback use when a staging deploy follows another one, and what does production rollback look like after promotion, when the SSM tags are already written? Is there any automatic path back after production is promoted and later turns out bad? (author: Staging: rollback uses previous_tag, which the staging deploy that just ran wrote from the tag current before it. That is the build that was on staging before the newer run, and rollback does not change previous_tag, so a second rollback goes to the same tag. Production after promotion: the pipeline has no step that goes back, and the brief defines none. Running deploy.sh rollback production would need a person or a CI job, and the brief rules out laptop deploys, so the path is unknown. It is listed under Open questions.)
